description:
docs/guides/stability.md (ADR-0010) promises, within a major version: a valid kernel keeps compiling and keeps its meaning; error codes keep their names, a rejection keeps its code, a code is never reused, a code whose construct becomes valid is retired and stays in the catalogue marked retired; the public API keeps names, arities and meaning; renames go through a deprecation. Today only meaning is checked (agreement with Elixir). Acceptance, codes over time, the API surface and deprecation have no test: the docs examples move with the code, and retired codes are a comment in lib/defk/errors.ex.

Approach: freeze what each release shipped as committed files under test/stability/<version>/, taken from the release tag, and check every later commit against them in mix ci. Frozen files are never edited; a release adds a directory.

Steps:
- frozen kernel corpus (acceptance + results)
- code ledger with a retired: field, retired codes in the catalogue
- frozen rejection corpus (needs the ledger)
- public API snapshot
- deprecation helper (before the first rename)
- process: CODEOWNERS on test/stability/, PR template line, CHANGELOG rule (after the four checks)

```mermaid
graph LR
    corpus[kernel corpus] --> proc[process]
    ledger[code ledger] --> rej[rejection corpus]
    rej --> proc
    api[API snapshot] --> proc
    dep[deprecation helper]
```

Done when the four checks run in mix ci against test/stability/0.1.0/, the deprecation helper exists with a test, and the process step is in place.

comments.text: PR #7 adds CHANGELOG lines for its changes to promised surfaces (enum-reduce, enum-find, raise-message); see the PR for the judgement calls.

Done: PRs #8 (kernel corpus), #9 (API snapshot), #10 (code ledger, retired codes), #11 (deprecation helper), #12 (rejection corpus), #13 (CODEOWNERS, PR template, release step) all merged into main; the four checks run in mix ci against test/stability/0.1.0/.

title: Stability promise: check it mechanically in mix ci
